newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Consultant sees higher Russian grain imports.
newsitem.headline: Consultant sees higher Russian grain imports.

text.p: Russian grain imports may reach six to eight million tonnes in 1996/97 (July/June), including four to five million tonnes of food grains, private agricultural consulatant Andrei Sizov said on Thursday.
Imports totalled just over five million tonnes in 1995/96.
The increase, slightly higher than a recent Sizov forecast, was expected despite a further fall in feed usage due to a decline in livestock numbers.

"Contrary to official statements that Russia would import only feeds, we say food grain imports will account for the major part of imports," Sizov, director general of SovEcon Ltd, told an Agra Europe grains conference.
Sizov told Reuters the latest forecast was about in line with earlier projections. The increase reflected low domestic grain sales and high local prices for food grains and flour.
Imports, especially of wheat, wheat flour and rye, rose sharply in the first two months of 1996/97, compared with the year-ago period.
Most of Russia's grain imports will be supplied by CIS countries, notably Kazakhstan.

Sizov said the Russian government was unlikely to start centralised grain imports this marketing year because of budgetary pressures. Instead it was likely to push commercial banks to provide credit lines for imports.
"It's quite a new phenomenon for Russia," Sizov said.
Sizov noted other trends in Russian grain trade, such as a decline in wheat and flour imports from CIS countries, notably from the Ukraine.
Russia was also diversifying imports, seeking supplies notably from India, Finland, Sweden and Germany.
